mechanisms.description: Lean proves model properties. This coverage comes from Rust tests that compare results with the executable Lean models.

mechanisms.name: Kani (Rust tests)
mechanisms.description: Coverage from ordinary Rust tests of functions with Kani harnesses.

mechanisms.name: Unit tests
mechanisms.description: Tests of individual functions and protocol rules.

mechanisms.name: Property tests (Hegel)
mechanisms.description: Generated inputs and histories, including real-repository end-to-end search.

mechanisms.name: Race scenarios
mechanisms.description: Deliberately interleaved operations on several repository copies.

mechanisms.name: End-to-end smoke
mechanisms.description: The short end-to-end search run in the default test profile.

mechanisms.name: Fuzzing
mechanisms.description: Coverage-guided inputs with decoder and store-integrity checks.

mechanisms.name: Fault injection
mechanisms.description: Broken links, lost or malformed replies, interrupted processes, and fault-suite regressions.

mechanisms.name: Integration tests
mechanisms.description: Real repositories and services exercised together, including storage and translation.

mechanisms.name: Transport contracts
mechanisms.description: The same behavioural contract checked against the transport implementations.

mechanisms.name: CLI tests
mechanisms.description: The real command-line program, daemons and hubs exercised as separate processes.

claims.title: Published history is complete
claims.detail: A hub publishes a head only with its ancestor operations and objects present.

claims.title: Machines eventually agree
claims.detail: After users stop and communication recovers, the policy makes progress to agreement.

claims.title: Sync does not echo endlessly
claims.detail: Modeled realization does not invent operations; legitimate merges are accounted for separately.

claims.title: Dropped operations stay dropped
claims.detail: Replicated abandonment and reconciliation must not revive a dropped head.

claims.title: A remade hub can rejoin agreement
claims.detail: The extended model covers a hub returning to an older head or being recreated empty.

claims.title: History survives translation
claims.detail: Local and canonical operations retain their meaning through translation and realization.

claims.title: Concurrent merge parents are retained
claims.detail: An advance beside concurrent local heads retains the exact maximal parent set.

claims.title: Abandonment preserves a concurrent fetch
claims.detail: The contracted survivor graph and saved expected ref values meet at realization.

claims.title: Imports do not spuriously revert work
claims.detail: Replicated git bookkeeping must not look like a new git edit that undoes a bookmark.

claims.title: Conflicted refs use the right history
claims.detail: History walking chooses an expected ref value consistently under operation renaming.

claims.title: Distributed conflicts match jj
claims.detail: A conflict or divergence should be explained by jj merging the same operations.

claims.title: Chunk retries preserve the blob
claims.detail: The receiver keeps a contiguous prefix, ignores overlaps, and verifies completed content.

claims.title: Hostile chunk offsets cannot overflow
claims.detail: Any prefix, offset and chunk length must give the correct extension boundary.

claims.title: Chunk windows advance correctly
claims.detail: Each window begins at the requested offset and ends at the blob end or window limit.

claims.title: Slow transfers finish
claims.detail: Each attempt goes on where the last left off, and blobs stay while chunks of them move.

claims.title: Payload budgets leave envelope room
claims.detail: The size allowance must remain sufficient across payload limits offered by a hub.

claims.title: Malformed peer bytes are checked
claims.detail: Frames, envelopes and bundles must decode or refuse safely under their stated properties.

claims.title: Imported content matches its identity
claims.detail: Import must not leave operations or views stored under an identity their contents do not have.

claims.title: A forgotten copy returns only with work
claims.detail: Forgetting a copy hides its workspaces without destroying its work.

claims.title: Workspace names remain distinct
claims.detail: Machine prefixes avoid each other and this machine’s own workspace names.

claims.title: A duplicate is not mistaken for the copy
claims.detail: A repository’s key and identity decide which moved or copied directory the daemon accepts.

claims.title: Torn append logs do not invent records
claims.detail: Damaged tails must read whole records correctly or detect damage.

claims.title: A damaged hub is detected and remade
claims.detail: A damaged store opens correctly or is identified as corrupt, allowing it to be recreated.

claims.title: Nodes recover from wrong replies
claims.detail: Well-formed but false hub replies must not trap a node permanently.

claims.title: Interrupted syncs recover
claims.detail: Crashes and partial network exchanges should allow subsequent convergence.

claims.title: The daemon discovers new repositories
claims.detail: The running daemon must notice and serve repositories that become available.

claims.title: The quick start works as written
claims.detail: The first-use guide is exercised through commands and real daemons.

claims.title: Messages remain reviewable
claims.detail: Inline output snapshots make user-visible changes explicit in review.

claims.title: Changes in jj are noticed early
claims.detail: The nightly jj-main job builds and runs the suite against jj’s development branch.

evidence.detail: Closure is proved for reachable model states.
Rust steps and state are compared with the executable model.
Checks safety directly on the Rust state, independently of the oracle.
Removing the closure guard is documented as caught by invariants and conformance.
A well-founded progress measure establishes policy termination.
Policy, uploads and progress measures are compared with the oracle.
Real-repository histories are driven to a fixed point and checked for agreement.
Sync steps preserve the operation universe.
The protocol harness checks steps against the model.
Retranslation makes no extra canonical operation at convergence.
Invariant and convergence proofs include dropped sets and supersedes.
The executable supersede model checks adoption, publication and dropped heads.
A node advancing to a dropped head is documented as detected through HeadsOK.
An extended invariant and convergence result cover hub regression.
The remake rule maps to regression to root and forgetting unstored history.
The real-repository search can restart the hub after dropping head-log entries.
Real-repository translation examples exercise the integration boundary.
Retranslates without caches and checks parent forms and realization round trips.
Advancing then merging the exact concurrent set is a reachable model run.
Observes published canonical heads in real repositories and compares them with the oracle.
A boundary theorem connects contracted heads and one-ref realization.
Checks exact merge parents, no dropped ancestor, the fetched ref and subsequent convergence.
The per-machine ref model states the no-spurious-revert property.
Pins laws of jj import/export on which the model relies.
Concrete fetch, restore and realization races pin regressions.
Audits each ref import against the git moves and jj exceptions that explain it.
Agreement, termination and import-agreement boundary are modeled.
Generated finite operation histories are compared with the oracle.
Per-machine ref behavior is checked against the model and jj laws.
An independent jj repository replays the hub history and compares merge outcomes.
The prefix receiver refines the chunk model, with safety and liveness results.
Real receiver steps are checked against the Lean oracle.
Faulted transfers exercise real multi-window blobs.
Symbolic Rust inputs include offsets near u64::MAX.
Checks Rust window arithmetic with a positive-chunk precondition and explicit unwind limit.
Concrete transfer examples check the integration path.
The Kani harness proves the allowance bound; a unit example pins that it fits.
A full chunk fits at the minimum payload limit.
Admitted frames round-trip byte for byte.
Admitted messages round-trip and trailing bytes are refused.
Admitted bundle records round-trip with and without compression.
Malformed requests and replies are injected into real sessions.
Correct and incorrect hashes reach import validation and store-integrity checks.
Whole records, deltas, duplicate and changed bytes exercise canonical import.
Presence is specified over operation histories.
Generated histories compare the implementation with the presence oracle.
Real-repository races check forgetting and return through fresh work.
Rules forget copies, expire idle copies and create fresh work.
The naming rule is injective under its stated inputs.
Generated clashes are checked against the names oracle.
Shared names and machine identities are exercised in real repositories.
Moved, copied, deleted and replaced repositories are modeled.
The decisions and daemon pre-sync check are compared with the copies oracle.
Generated damage includes truncation, zeros, garbling and concurrent appends.
Parser properties check whole lines and damaged tails.
Generated damage checks heads and backend recognition.
Store integration examples check concrete behavior.
The core state machine explores false replies and recovery.
Real-repository recovery cases run in the CI profile.
A scripted link can die or stall partway through a session.
The search can crash while realizations are being written, lose caches or lose a reply.
A command-level test checks discovery through real services.
The documented first-use sequence is an executable scenario.
Command output is pinned with inline snapshots during a real lifecycle.
Checks that download bounds cannot overflow and that completion agrees with the blob size.
Real upload and download windows, cut short by deadlines, are checked against the Lean oracle.
Chunks renew the blobs they touch as the timed model's renewal says.
Calls slow enough for the hub to sweep old blobs still finish, moving no chunk twice.
